output.reason: A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection today (probing for depth/abscess, assessment of infection extent, possible swab and antibiotic treatment), which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please get your foot looked at in person today — an urgent care, your diabetes or foot clinic, or an emergency department if nothing else is available. A spreading red, swollen, tender wound on the sole in someone with diabetes needs the wound examined and probed and likely antibiotics started. Go to the ED sooner if you develop fever, chills, spreading redness, pus, black skin or a foul smell. Keep weight off that foot meanwhile.
differential: Cellulitis / early diabetic foot infection of the plantar wound
Deeper abscess or wound extending to deeper tissue

redFlags.concern: Spreading erythema and swelling around foot wound
redFlags.quote: the skin around it is red and a little swollen
tender when I press on it

redFlags.concern: Neuropathy or sensation loss in feet

output.vitalSigns: No temperature, heart rate, blood pressure or glucose values reported; the patient states "No fever" but no measurement method or whether any vitals were taken is known.
output.evidenceLimitations: Only consumer health summaries and an ED reference synthesis were available; neither establishes a telehealth-eligible assessment for this patient's wound depth or infection severity.

citations.claim: Consumer guidance advises prompt in-person review for red, warm or painful skin on the feet in diabetes.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; not a specialty guideline and does not set an exact timeframe or treatment.

citations.claim: Serious diabetic foot problems can develop quickly, supporting same-day rather than deferred assessment.
citations.limitation: General education about diabetic foot risk, not a diagnosis of this patient's wound.
